title: Health Externalities and Policy: The Role of Social Preferences
eligible_reason: Staggered binary Lockdown_ct indicator exists (country- or state-level lockdown dates), but every main-text specification (Tables 2-4, 36 columns) adds (i) Lockdown x continuous regional social-preference measure, (ii) a second staggered treatment Lifting_ct (and its interaction), (iii) time-varying controls (7-day moving averages of cases and deaths per capita at t-1, log Google Trends at t-1), and in cols 4-6 a third indicator Voluntary_ct, in cols 7-9 interactions with cases, density and foreign-born share, in cols 10-12 a stay-at-home indicator that switches on and off. No main-text column is a plain TWFE on the binary treatment. The only plain TWFE (ln mobility on Lockdown_ct + city FE + date FE) appears solely as a Goodman-Bacon decomposition in Online Appendix B, Table B.1, without standard errors.
design_notes: Unit = city-day (258 cities, 23 countries, Jan 22 - Jun 30, 2020). Lockdown_ct = 1 from first day of official country-wide (state/province-wide for US, Brazil, Canada) lockdown; Lifting_ct = 1 from first lifting date. FE: city, date, country-by-month. SE double-clustered city and date. Outcomes: ln(Apple Mobility walking / driving / transit index). Dates from Wikipedia, NASHP, NYT; stay-at-home indicator from OxCGRT. Text screened is the June 2021 ECONtribute DP No. 109 working paper (EconStor), not the published MS version; table numbering and data statement may differ in print.
estimators_reported: TWFE static with continuous-moderator interactions and time-varying controls

specs.outcome: ln walking / ln driving / ln transit (Apple Mobility)
specs.treatment_definition: post first official lockdown date in country c (state/province for US, BR, CA); Lifting_ct = post first lifting date
specs.fe: city FE, date FE, country x month FE
specs.controls: Lockdown x Preference_g, Lifting x Preference_g (continuous, time-invariant region measure); 7-day MA cases per capita (t-1), 7-day MA deaths per capita (t-1), ln Google Trends 'Coronavirus' (t-1)
specs.sample: countries with >=2 cities in different regions; N=38,467 / 39,075 / 26,352
specs.reported_location: Table 2, cols 1-3 (also Table 3 and Table 4 cols 1-3 with Patience / Neg. reciprocity)
specs.exclusion_reason: ineligible_with_controls: time-varying controls (cases, deaths, Google Trends) + continuous treatment-by-moderator interaction + additional staggered treatment (Lifting). No no-controls version in main text.
specs.notes: Headline coefficient of interest is the interaction Lockdown x Preference, not the binary treatment itself.

specs.controls: as cols 1-3 plus Voluntary_ct and Voluntary x Preference
specs.exclusion_reason: ineligible_with_controls; three indicators plus continuous interactions

specs.controls: as cols 1-3 plus Lockdown/Lifting x cases per capita (time-varying), x population density, x share new foreigners
specs.sample: subsample with density and foreign-born data; N=19,608 / 19,608 / 14,592
specs.exclusion_reason: ineligible_with_controls; treatment x time-varying covariate interactions

specs.treatment_definition: stay-at-home requirement in place at date t; switches on and off
specs.controls: Stay-at-home x Preference; cases, deaths, Google Trends
specs.exclusion_reason: ineligible_with_controls; treatment switches off; continuous interaction

specs.outcome: mobility (walking / driving / transit; transformation not stated, presumably ln)
specs.reported_location: Online Appendix B, Table B.1 (not main text)
specs.exclusion_reason: appendix only; no SE reported; not a main-text specification
specs.notes: This is the only plain staggered TWFE in the paper. Weights: treated vs never-treated 0.745 / 0.744 / 0.837, so never-treated countries exist in the sample.

screener_notes: Flags (ft_goodman_bacon, ft_staggered, ft_two_way_fixed_effects) are driven by Online Appendix B. Not eligible because the binary treatment never appears without time-varying controls and continuous interactions in the main text. Inputs (Apple Mobility, Global Preferences Survey, OxCGRT, JHU, Google Trends, OECD) were public at the time; Apple Mobility data were discontinued in April 2022 so re-collection is not possible without the authors' extract. No replication package in the project frame; published MS version not checked.
